lead: No natural product has strong evidence in fibromyalgia. A 24-week placebo-controlled trial of CBD tablets in 200 people found it relieved pain less than placebo (grade: Negative). Vitamin D, magnesium, SAMe and acetyl-L-carnitine have small or mixed randomized trials (grade B), and no human studies of turmeric or curcumin in fibromyalgia were found.

grade_key.A: Meta-analysis, or at least 2 randomized trials with low risk of bias and a consistent benefit
grade_key.B: 1 good randomized trial, or several randomized trials with mixed results
grade_key.C: Observational studies, small pilots or open-label trials only
grade_key.Negative: Randomized trials found no benefit over placebo

disclaimer: This page summarizes published research. It is not medical advice. Talk to a clinician before starting any supplement, especially if you take other medicines.

products.name: Acetyl-L-carnitine
products.summary: A multicentre trial randomized 102 people to acetyl-L-carnitine or placebo. Both groups improved for the first 6 weeks; by week 10 the acetyl-L-carnitine group had better tender-point, depression and musculoskeletal pain scores. A smaller trial compared it with duloxetine, with no placebo group, and found improvements with both.
products.safety_interactions: The placebo-controlled trial reported that treatment was well tolerated. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: L-carnitine and acetyl-L-carnitine
general_safety.short: In neuropathy trials, adverse events with acetyl-L-carnitine were similar to placebo; L-carnitine taken for 12 to 24 weeks raised blood TMAO, a compound linked to atherosclerosis.

citations.label: Rossini et al., 2007, Clin Exp Rheumatol
citations.title: Double-blind, multicenter trial comparing acetyl l-carnitine with placebo in the treatment of fibromyalgia patients.

citations.label: Leombruni et al., 2015, Clin Exp Rheumatol
citations.title: A randomised controlled trial comparing duloxetine and acetyl L-carnitine in fibromyalgic patients: preliminary data.

products.name: Magnesium
products.summary: A review of the evidence on magnesium with malic acid found one randomized trial and concluded the combination makes little or no difference to pain or depressive symptoms. A separate 1-month randomized trial of magnesium against placebo found no difference in its main outcome, stress, although pain scores fell more with magnesium as a secondary outcome.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Magnesium
general_safety.short: Oral magnesium mainly causes gastrointestinal effects such as diarrhoea; severe high blood magnesium occurs almost only in people with substantially reduced kidney function.

citations.label: Ferreira et al., 2019, Medwave
citations.title: Magnesium and malic acid supplement for fibromyalgia.

citations.label: Macian et al., 2022, Nutrients
citations.title: Short-Term Magnesium Therapy Alleviates Moderate Stress in Patients with Fibromyalgia: A Randomized Double-Blind Clinical Trial.

products.name: S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe)
products.summary: Three small placebo-controlled trials were published between 1987 and 1997. A 6-week trial of oral SAMe in 44 people found less pain, fatigue and morning stiffness than with placebo, but no change in tender points. A crossover trial in 17 people found fewer tender points. A 10-day trial of intravenous SAMe in 34 people found no effect on its main outcome.
products.safety_interactions: In the oral trial, side effects did not differ between SAMe and placebo. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe)
general_safety.short: Dropout rates in depression trials were similar to placebo or antidepressants. A review says it is contraindicated in bipolar disorder; a case report describes mania with an SSRI.

citations.label: Jacobsen et al., 1991, Scand J Rheumatol
citations.title: Oral S-adenosylmethionine in primary fibromyalgia. Double-blind clinical evaluation.

citations.label: Tavoni et al., 1987, Am J Med
citations.title: Evaluation of S-adenosylmethionine in primary fibromyalgia. A double-blind crossover study.

citations.label: Volkmann et al., 1997, Scand J Rheumatol
citations.title: Double-blind, placebo-controlled cross-over study of intravenous S-adenosyl-L-methionine in patients with fibromyalgia.

products.name: Vitamin D
products.summary: Two meta-analyses compared vitamin D with placebo or a control group. One, limited to randomized trials, pooled 5 studies with 315 people and found lower Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire scores but no difference in pain on a visual scale. The other, with 4 studies in each analysis, found lower pain scores and called for better trials.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Vitamin D
general_safety.short: Long-term supplementation raised the risk of high blood calcium and high urine calcium in trials, but not kidney stones; toxicity from extremely high doses is rare but serious.

citations.label: Qu et al., 2022, Expert Rev Clin Pharmacol
citations.title: The efficacy of vitamin D in treatment of fibromyalgia: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled studies and systematic review.

citations.label: Ilari et al., 2025, Nutrients
citations.title: Does Vitamin D Supplementation Impact Fibromyalgia-Related Pain? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

products.name: Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10)
products.summary: A 40-day randomized trial in 20 people found lower Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire and pain scores with CoQ10 than with placebo. A randomized crossover trial of a combined CoQ10, tryptophan and magnesium supplement, with two 3-month periods and 89 people completing it, found no benefit on its main outcome, fatigue; sleep quality and functional impact scores improved within the supplement group, and pain fell in both groups.
products.safety_interactions: In the combined-supplement trial, adverse events were mild and similar between groups. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trials.

general_safety.name: Coenzyme Q10
general_safety.short: Few adverse events were reported in trials. A case report describes reduced warfarin response while taking CoQ10.

citations.label: Cordero et al., 2013, Antioxid Redox Signal
citations.title: Can coenzyme q10 improve clinical and molecular parameters in fibromyalgia?

citations.label: Rosselló Aubach et al., 2025, J Diet Suppl
citations.title: Effects of Coenzyme Q10, Tryptophan, and Magnesium Supplementation on Fatigue in Patients with Fibromyalgia - A Randomized Trial.

products.name: Melatonin
products.summary: One 8-week trial, described as double-blind and placebo-controlled although no placebo arm is listed, compared melatonin alone, the antidepressant fluoxetine alone, and the two combined. Fibromyalgia impact scores fell from baseline in the combination groups, and the authors concluded melatonin alone was also effective. A systematic review of 4 studies with 98 people found benefits in all of them but large differences between the studies.
products.safety_interactions: The systematic review found no major adverse events reported. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: Melatonin
general_safety.short: Trial adverse events were few and mostly mild (daytime sleepiness, headache, dizziness); long-term data are limited. Drugs acting on CYP1A2 may slow its breakdown.

citations.label: Hussain et al., 2011, J Pineal Res
citations.title: Adjuvant use of melatonin for treatment of fibromyalgia.

citations.label: Hemati et al., 2020, Complement Ther Clin Pract
citations.title: Melatonin in the treatment of fibromyalgia symptoms: A systematic review.

products.name: THC-containing cannabis and nabilone
products.summary: A Cochrane review found two small trials of nabilone, a synthetic cannabinoid, with 72 participants in total, rated the evidence very low quality and found no convincing evidence of benefit. A 2026 meta-analysis pooling 2 randomized and 10 observational studies reported lower pain with cannabinoids, but rated the evidence low quality. An 8-week trial of a THC-rich cannabis oil in 17 women reported better Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire scores than placebo.
products.safety_interactions: The Cochrane review found nabilone poorly tolerated in fibromyalgia. The meta-analysis listed dizziness, dry mouth and drowsiness as common side effects, with serious adverse effects rare. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited studies.

general_safety.name: THC-containing cannabis and cannabinoids
general_safety.short: Trials show more short-term adverse events, including dizziness, drowsiness, confusion and hallucinations, and more withdrawals due to adverse events than placebo.

citations.label: Walitt et al., 2016, Cochrane Database Syst Rev
citations.title: Cannabinoids for fibromyalgia.

citations.label: Lam et al., 2026, Pain Physician
citations.title: Analgesic Effect of Cannabinoids for Fibromyalgia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

citations.label: Chaves et al., 2020, Pain Med
citations.title: Ingestion of a THC-Rich Cannabis Oil in People with Fibromyalgia: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial.

products.name: Cannabidiol (CBD)
products.summary: In a 24-week randomized trial in 200 people with fibromyalgia, 50 mg of plant-derived CBD a day was compared with placebo. Pain fell less with CBD than with placebo, by 0.7 points on a 0 to 10 scale, and the authors concluded the results do not support CBD as a pain-relieving supplement in fibromyalgia.
products.safety_interactions: In that trial, adverse events were generally mild and evenly spread between the CBD and placebo groups. Interactions with medicines were not reported in the cited trial.

general_safety.name: Cannabidiol (CBD)
general_safety.short: Raises the chance of liver enzyme elevation, especially at high doses or with antiseizure drugs. Raises a clobazam metabolite and may interact with drugs using CYP450 enzymes.

citations.label: Rasmussen et al., 2026, Ann Rheum Dis
citations.title: Cannabidiol versus placebo in patients with fibromyalgia: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, single-centre trial.

products.name: Turmeric and curcumin
products.summary: No randomized, observational or pilot studies of turmeric or curcumin in people with fibromyalgia were found in a PubMed search on 23 November 2026. Claims about it in fibromyalgia rest on studies of other conditions or laboratory work.
products.safety_interactions: No safety data found in the cited trials, because no fibromyalgia trials were found.

general_safety.name: Turmeric and curcumin
general_safety.short: Case series link turmeric supplements to liver injury, sometimes severe. Curcumin may alter levels of some drugs, including anticoagulants, mostly in non-clinical studies.
